verification: Objective achieved: Backlog authority follow-up: runtime diagnostics and quotas
acceptance_criteria: The authority failure gauge reflects endpoint failures and exposes only bounded, low-cardinality reasons.
The authority timeout is derived from configuration and is covered by a failing-then-passing regression test.
Reservation responses echo reservation_id so callers can correlate retries without exposing tenant data.
ID-space exhaustion raises a quota/alarm signal and returns a fixed safe reason instead of a zeroed success.

BLOCKER: AC-4 not implemented: the new alert `ProductForgeBacklogIDSpaceExhausted` reads `edp_backlog_reservation_exhausted_total`, but nothing in the diff increments that metric — the alert can never fire.
AC-4: no exhaustion path exists — `Reserve`/`backlogReserve` add no quota check, no fixed safe reason code, and no `TestAuthorityIDSpaceExhaustionFailsClosed`; a zeroed success remains possible.

AC-2 evidence missing: the design-mandated `TestAuthorityTimeoutComesFromConfig` is absent; `TestBacklogWithTimeoutUsesConfiguredDuration` only asserts the struct field and never proves the timeout reaches `set_config('statement_timeout', ...)` or is sourced from config (no failing-then-passing red evidence, CL-010).
MAJOR: AC-1 has no test: `TestAuthorityFailureMetricUsesBoundedReasons` is not in the diff; the failure gauge/reason path is unchanged, so boundedness is unproven.
`WithTimeout` mutates the receiver and returns the same pointer; safe only because callers construct fresh stores — a reused `BacklogStore` shared across goroutines becomes a data race.
`WithTimeout` silently ignores `d <= 0`, converting misconfiguration into a hidden default instead of a startup failure.
No observability on the exhaustion/id-space path (no log line, no metric) despite the paging alert depending on it.

Statement timeout is set from `DBTimeout` while the caller already wraps the same value in `context.WithTimeout`; no assertion that the SQL-level timeout fires before ctx cancellation in the reserve path.
MINOR: `TestReservationResponseEchoesID` tests the helper in isolation, not the HTTP handler contract (status/code/tenant leakage), so AC-3 is only weakly covered.
`reservationResponse` echoes whatever `b.ReservationID` holds, including empty/unvalidated values; retry-correlation semantics rely on upstream validation not asserted here.
Test-name/evidence drift between design contract and delivered tests (AC-2, AC-3) undermines traceability.
NIT: `defaultStatementTimeout` duplicates the config-derived value with no single source of truth.
`fmt.Sprintf("%dms", ms)` string-building in a SQL path could be a typed duration/int parameter.
SUMMARY: The change partially satisfies AC-2 and AC-3 but leaves AC-1 and AC-4 substantively unmet; the shipped Prometheus alert is dead because its metric is never emitted.
Highest risk: a paging alert that silently never fires plus continued zeroed-success on ID-space exhaustion — false operational assurance.
Second risk: the timeout is now configurable but not proven by the required regression tests, and the mutating `WithTimeout` builder is a latent concurrency hazard.
Recommend blocking merge until exhaustion metric+reason+test land and the config-driven timeout test asserts the emitted statement, not just a field.

MAJOR: AC-1: `TestAuthorityFailureMetricUsesBoundedReasons` only exercises the pure `authorityReasonCode` map; nothing asserts the authority failure gauge/metric actually increments on an endpoint failure, so "gauge reflects endpoint failures" remains unproven (prior disposition overstated).

AC-2: `TestAuthorityTimeoutComesFromConfig` hardcodes `2345 * time.Millisecond` and calls `WithTimeout` directly; it proves propagation to `set_config` but not that the value is derived from configuration (no config loader/env path exercised).

AC-4: `TestAuthorityIDSpaceExhaustionFailsClosed` only asserts the `edpdata` sentinel; no test asserts the service returns a fixed safe reason with a non-2xx status and that `edp_backlog_reservation_exhausted_total` (the alarm input) is incremented on the exhaustion path.
MINOR: AC-3: only the test name changed; `TestAuthorityResponseEchoesReservationID` still tests the helper in isolation with no HTTP-level assertion on status/code/absence of tenant fields.
`authorityReasonCode` catch-all maps any unrecognized error (e.g. code bug, wrapped deadline) to `db_unavailable`; the new test case locks in that conflation, weakening diagnosis separation.
`fakeStore.Exec` still discards args while `fakeTx.Exec` records them; the divergent fakes can silently hide a missing statement timeout on non-transactional paths.

Design `ac_evidence`/`test_matrix` cite `go/edpsvc/main_test.go::TestAuthorityTimeoutComesFromConfig`, but the test now lives in `go/edpdata/edpdata_test.go` — evidence path drift breaks traceability.
NIT: Timeout assertion relies on `execs[0][0]` ordering and `fmt.Sprint(...)=="2345ms"`, so it is brittle to arg order and duration formatting changes.
The Authority call's error is discarded (`_`); the test could pass while Authority still returns a failure after the exec.
Exhaustion test assumes the first `Query` returns the counter row; multi-query Reserve implementations would silently break it.
SUMMARY: Delta cleanly centralizes exhaustion handling (single metric/log/response helper, no behavior change) and adds real regression coverage for timeout propagation and fail-closed exhaustion.
Remaining gaps are evidentiary: AC-1 gauge increment, AC-2 config derivation, AC-4 service-level safe reason + alarm metric are still only partially proven.
No integrity, security, or language-rule blockers found; test fakes and evidence-path drift should be tightened before claiming the ACs closed.

MAJOR: AC-4: `TestReservationExhaustedFailsClosedWithAlarm` invokes `s.reservationExhausted` directly; it never exercises `backlogReserve` with an `ErrIDSpaceExhausted` result, so the endpoint could fail to raise the alarm or return a zeroed success while the test passes.

AC-1: the new endpoint metric assertion lives in `TestBacklogAuthorityFailsClosed`, which skips unless `PF_RUNTIME_DSN` is set; non-gated evidence still only calls `authorityReasonCode`, so standard CI does not prove the gauge reflects endpoint failures.
MINOR: AC-1 evidence asserts `edp_backlog_authority_errors_total` (counter) while the AC says gauge; confirm intended metric semantics or update the contract.
AC-2: `TestAuthorityTimeoutComesFromConfig` manually applies `cfg.DBTimeout` via `NewBacklog(nil).WithTimeout(...)`; it does not prove `edpsvc` wires the configured timeout into the authority store.
AC-3: `TestBacklogReserveEchoesIDWithDB` only checks for an exact `tenant` key; a response leaking `tenant_id` or nested tenant fields would pass.
`authorityReasonCode`'s new substring markers, especially `"db"`, classify errors by message text; driver/message changes can silently reclassify failures and weaken diagnostics.
Design `ac_evidence`/`test_matrix` still cite the old AC-1/AC-4 tests and do not reference the new endpoint/alarm tests, so traceability is out of sync.
NIT: `TestBacklogTimeoutPropagatesToStatementTimeout` couples the timeout regression to `ErrAuthoritySchema`; unrelated schema-detection changes can break a timeout test.
`StatementTimeout` is an exported test-only accessor on the production store; consider an unexported/test helper to avoid widening the package API.
`TestBacklogReserveEchoesIDWithDB` uses wall-clock nano IDs and leaves reservations in the shared runtime DB; repeated runs accumulate test data.
SUMMARY: The delta resolves several prior test gaps and correctly adds JSON tags so `reservation_id` is decoded.
The main residual risk is AC-4 endpoint wiring: the new alarm test bypasses `backlogReserve`.
AC-1 endpoint metric evidence is DB-gated, and the new `authorityReasonCode` substring heuristic is brittle.
AC-2/AC-3 tests prove pieces but not full service wiring or broad tenant-leak absence.

MAJOR: AC-4/delta `main_test.go::TestReservationExhaustedFailsClosedWithAlarm`: it asserts only the 409 body, not that the quota/alarm signal was raised; the "raises a quota/alarm signal" half of AC-4 remains unproven at the endpoint (prior disposition only partly actioned).

`edp_backlog_authority_endpoint_ok` is a latch updated only on request: it starts/returns 0 before any success and stays 0 indefinitely after one failure on this operator-only endpoint, so an `endpoint_ok == 0` rule alerts on deploy and never clears until a manual call succeeds.

Same gauge is set to 0 for non-availability reasons (`migration_missing`, `row_missing`), conflating configuration/schema faults with endpoint availability; alerting cannot distinguish without duplicating the bounded reason label.
MINOR: `authorityReasonCode` drops `"database"`/`"db"` while adding the broad `"driver"`: `unknown driver ...` now reports `db_unavailable` (masks config bugs) and `cannot connect to database` falls to `internal_error`; still message-substring classification, only partially addressing the prior MINOR.

`reserveBacklog` calls the `func(tenant string)` factory with `""` while `backlogForTenant` passes a real tenant; the seam's contract is inconsistent and a future factory that binds by tenant would silently reserve unbound.
AC-3/delta `TestBacklogReserveEchoesIDWithDB` scans only top-level keys for `tenant`; a nested map/array field (`meta.tenant_id`) would still leak and pass.
`TestAuthorityFailureMetricUsesBoundedReasons` asserts an exact counter value of `1`, which is flaky if `limits.Metrics` is shared across servers/tests rather than per-`testServer`.

`TestAuthorityTimeoutComesFromConfig` now exercises `store.BindTenant(s.st, ...)` with a nil `s.st`; it silently depends on `BindTenant` tolerating nil and still does not prove tenant binding reaches the query (CL-011).
`backlogForTenant`/`reserveBacklog` duplicate the `NewBacklog(...).WithTimeout(s.cfg.DBTimeout)` construction and factory branch; centralise to keep construction semantics in one place.
NIT: `Test...WithAlarm` name implies an alarm assertion that the test does not make; rename or add the alarm metric/quota assertion.
`TestBacklogTimeoutPropagatesToStatementTimeout`'s positional 3-result `queries` fixture is brittle to any change in authority query order/count.
`StatementTimeout()` is carried on the production `backlogStore` interface solely for the config test; a test-local accessor would avoid widening the seam.
SUMMARY: Delta closes the prior endpoint/factory gaps for AC-1 and AC-2 and improves AC-3's tenant-leak check; no data-loss, secret or RLS regressions found.
Remaining risks: AC-4's alarm signal is still unasserted at the endpoint, and the new `endpoint_ok` gauge is a last-request latch that can produce persistent false alerts.
Reason-code classification remains string-based and was arguably weakened by the `db`→`driver` marker swap.

MAJOR: `authorityReasonCode` default branch removes the `"57014"`/`"timeout"` string fallbacks: a Postgres statement timeout (`*pgconn.PgError` SQLSTATE 57014, not a `net.Error`) now reports `internal_error`, dropping the timeout diagnostic that CL-012 and AC-1 depend on. Add explicit 57014 mapping + test.

`errors.As(err, &netErr)` precedes any `Timeout()` check, so a non-deadline net timeout (custom dialer) is reported `db_unavailable`; order/guard on `netErr.Timeout()` to keep `timeout` distinct from `db_unavailable`.

`checkBacklogAuthority` now writes `edp_backlog_authority_last_request_ok`: a transient DB blip at boot pins the "last request" gauge to 0 with no request made, so a `== 0` alert fires on deploy and clears only after a manual operator call — same false-alarm shape the prior MAJOR asked to remove.
MINOR: `backlogFor(tenant string, reserve bool)` silently discards `tenant` when `reserve` is true: a future caller passing a real tenant gets an unbound (no-RLS) store — the exact seam hazard this refactor closed for the factory. Prefer two named constructors.

Dropping the `"connection"`/`"refused"`/`"closed"`/`"driver"` markers narrows `db_unavailable`: pgconn "conn closed"/unexpected EOF, TLS and auth errors now surface as `internal_error`, under-reporting availability in the bounded reason set.
AC-1 evidence only proves the `last_request_ok == 0` case; no test asserts the gauge returns to 1 on a subsequent success, nor that the startup write does not leak into request semantics.

The new rules-file assertion is a substring check only (could match a comment) and no equivalent assertion covers the `endpoint_ok` → `last_request_ok` rename, so a stale rule name would silently never fire.
NIT: Reading `../../ops/prometheus/backlog-authority.rules.yml` by relative path couples a unit test to repo layout; breaks under alternate working dirs or packaging.
`hasTenantKey` treats any key containing "tenant" as a leak and inspects keys only, not values — over-broad false positives, blind to `{"owner": "tenant-a"}`.
SUMMARY: Net improvement: factory seam unified, gauge renamed with startup/request parity, recursive tenant-leak check, and alarm-rule evidence added.
Top risks: the reason-code rewrite regresses timeout classification (PG 57014 and net timeouts), and the shared request/startup gauge can page on deploy.
Recommend fixing reason precedence/57014 mapping and separating startup vs request gauges before merge; remaining items are coverage polish.

MAJOR: `authorityReasonCode` now classifies any error whose lowercased message contains `"tls"` or `"password authentication"` as `db_unavailable`; substring `"tls"` also matches unrelated words (e.g. "defaults", "results") — over-broad classification risks mislabeling genuine internal errors as availability failures and skewing the bounded reason diagnostics.
MINOR: `backlogReserve` changed to `s.reserveBacklog()` which calls `s.backlogFactory("", true)`; the empty tenant is now hard-coded inside the new helper rather than at the call site, removing the documented "admin-only, no tenant binding" context from the seam — a future factory caller may assume tenant scoping, so add a doc comment on `reserveBacklog` making the deliberate unbound store explicit.

`authorityBacklog`/`reserveBacklog` duplicate the `edpdata.NewBacklog(...).WithTimeout(s.cfg.DBTimeout)` construction; the timeout wiring is now expressed twice, so a future change to the default timeout/backlog constructor must be kept in sync in both helpers.

New test `TestAuthorityFailureMetricUsesBoundedReasons` mutates `s.backlogFactory` after the initial failure assertion and asserts recovery — good, but no test asserts that `reserveBacklog`'s unbound factory path (`tenant=""`) is exercised, leaving the reserve seam untested for the tenant-binding invariant.
NIT: The `57014`/`statement timeout` fallback is checked before `errors.As(err, &netErr)`; ordering is fine today but unreachable for `*pgconn.PgError` users — consider a dedicated `errors.As(&pgErr)` branch for clarity and to avoid string matching on `"57014"`.

`TestAuthorityFailureMetricUsesBoundedReasons` uses `strings.Contains(..., "edp_backlog_authority_errors_total{reason=\"internal_error\"}")` without the value; the earlier exact-value assertion was relaxed, weakening the metric-shape check.
SUMMARY: Delta resolves prior MAJORs (timeout precedence, request-only gauge, recovery assertion, textual markers) and cleanly splits `backlogFor` into `authorityBacklog`/`reserveBacklog`.
Main residual risk is the over-broad `"tls"` substring marker in `authorityReasonCode`, which can misclassify non-availability errors and pollute diagnostics; tighten the marker set.
Minor reuse/duplication between the two backlog helpers and an untested reserve seam are worth addressing but not blocking.

MAJOR: The tightened marker list now under-matches common connectivity failures (e.g. `tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: ...`, `dial tcp ...: i/o timeout`, `no pg_hba.conf entry`), which fall through to `internal_error`; if the `backlog-authority.rules.yml` alarm routes on `db_unavailable`, availability incidents are silently mis-routed (alarm lead-time regression). Confirm the rule keys on the aggregate series or add `x509`/`certificate` markers.
MINOR: `TestAuthorityFailureMetricUsesBoundedReasons` asserts `...reason="internal_error"} 1` via `strings.Contains`, which also matches `} 10`, `} 12`, `} 137`; the "exact value" check is still non-exact — assert `"} 1\n"` or parse the text exposition.

Narrowing `"tls"` -> `"tls handshake"` and `"password authentication"` -> `"password authentication failed"` silently changes classification of previously-tagged errors; no table-driven test locks the allow/deny boundary of the marker list, so future drift (over- or under-matching) is unguarded.

`newBacklog` centralises construction but the timeout default (`s.cfg.DBTimeout`) still has no assertion that the reserve path inherits the same configured timeout; only the authority path is covered by `TestAuthorityTimeoutComesFromConfig` per the AC matrix.
NIT: `t.Fatalf` is invoked from inside the `backlogFactory` closure; safe today only because the handler runs on the test goroutine — `t.Errorf` + a returned sentinel error would survive any future async/concurrent seam.
Marker list is an inline literal in `authorityReasonCode`; a package-level `var dbUnavailableMarkers` would make the classification boundary reviewable and reusable by tests.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly resolves the prior over-broad marker MAJOR, the duplicated constructor MINOR, and the missing reserve-seam assertion; all prior findings appear ACTIONED.
Residual risks: reason-marker under-matching can hide real availability failures from reason-scoped alarms, and the "exact value" metric assertion is still substring-based (matches 10/12/137).
No AC evidence removed by this delta; no language-rule, tenant-isolation, or schema concerns introduced.

MINOR: `dbUnavailableMarkers` now classifies any error containing `certificate` or `x509` as `db_unavailable`; non-connectivity failures such as certificate config/rotation errors would be mislabeled and can skew authority failure alarms.
The added marker cases are positive-only; no negative table case locks the broadened `certificate`/`x509` boundary, so future over-matching remains unguarded.
NIT: `dbUnavailableMarkers` is a mutable package-level slice; an immutable array or read-only accessor would better signal the classification table is not runtime-mutable.
SUMMARY: Delta resolves the prior marker/timeout/metric-exactness gaps and keeps authority reasons bounded; no AC-breaking regression is evident in the delta.
Main residual risk is over-broad substring classification (`certificate`, `x509`) reducing diagnostic precision and potentially causing false `db_unavailable` signals.

MINOR: New `x509.HostnameError` and `x509.CertificateInvalidError` branches are not exercised by tests; only `x509.UnknownAuthorityError` is covered, leaving two new classifiers unguarded against regression.

Typed `HostnameError`/`CertificateInvalidError` still map certificate configuration/rotation failures such as hostname mismatch or expired cert to `db_unavailable`, so the authority failure gauge can conflate TLS misconfiguration with a true DB endpoint outage.

Removing the `x509`/`certificate` string markers means plain-string TLS/certificate errors that do not wrap typed x509 errors now fall through to `internal_error`; no boundary test covers that fallback, reducing diagnostic fidelity for non-Go/proxy error paths.
NIT: The negative case only pins `"certificate rotation pending"`; add coverage for other removed marker forms such as bare `"x509"` to lock the narrowed classification boundary.
SUMMARY: The delta resolves the prior broad string-matching issue by switching to typed x509 classification and adds a negative boundary case.
No blockers found; residual risk is semantic misclassification of TLS configuration failures and incomplete test coverage for the newly added error types and string-fallback behavior.

MAJOR: TLS classification is now split by error form: typed x509 errors → `tls_error`, but plain-string `x509:` errors → `db_unavailable` via `dbUnavailableMarkers`. Same root cause yields two reasons, so alert rules keyed on `db_unavailable` will fire on TLS misconfig only through the untyped path, partially defeating the new `tls_error` distinction (AC-1 consistency).
MINOR: `"x509:"` is a loose substring marker matched anywhere in the message; unrelated text containing that token (driver/proxy wrappers, SQL fragments) is silently classified `db_unavailable`. Prefer prefix/anchored matching or typed-only classification.

Moving the statement-timeout string check after the typed x509 branch changes precedence with no test pinning it; add a case where text matches both a 57014/statement-timeout and a marker to lock ordering.
No test wraps a typed x509 error (`fmt.Errorf("...: %w", x509.UnknownAuthorityError{})`) to prove `errors.As` traversal still yields `tls_error` through the new branch order.
NIT: Mixing the `tls_error` concept with a `"x509:"` entry inside `dbUnavailableMarkers` obscures intent; a short comment or grouped marker set would make the boundary explicit.
SUMMARY: Delta is small, Go-only, and resolves the prior review findings (typed x509 coverage, fallback boundary, `tls_error` bucket); no blockers.
Top risk: inconsistent TLS reason classification between typed and stringified errors, which can misroute alerts and inflate/deflate the `tls_error` series unexpectedly.
Minor gaps: brittle substring marker and un-pinned classification precedence/wrapping behaviour.

MINOR: Delta removes `tls_error` from the allowlist but only changes one emitter; there is no assertion that no other code path (metric wiring, other `authorityReasonCode` branches) still returns the literal `tls_error`, so the bounded-reason guarantee is now unverified for the removed value.

`{fmt.Errorf("x509: legacy string"), "db_unavailable"}` still passes only through loose substring matching of `"x509:"`; the prior "anchor/typed-only" correction is not actually pinned by the delta's test evidence.

Collapsing certificate/CA/hostname failures into `db_unavailable` removes triage signal: alert rules and dashboards (including `ops/prometheus/backlog-authority.rules.yml` in this change set) can no longer route cert-expiry/CA-rotation to the identity/owner path, raising MTTR; confirm rule/docs coverage reflects the unified reason.
NIT: The declared AC-1 evidence is `TestAuthorityFailureMetricUsesBoundedReasons`, but the delta edits `TestAuthorityReasonCodesAreBounded`; naming drift makes evidence traceability harder than necessary.
The typed-x509 and wrapped-x509 cases now assert the same reason; a short comment grouping them as "TLS errors unify to db_unavailable" would make the intent explicit for future editors.
SUMMARY: Delta is a clean, reversible tightening: bounded reason set shrinks, typed/wrapped x509 unify to `db_unavailable`, and precedence against statement-timeout (`57014`) is explicitly pinned — prior findings appear resolved.

Remaining risks are observability/evidence-level, not correctness: no proof that `tls_error` is fully retired from all emitters, no pinned assertion on marker anchoring, and lost cert-vs-DB-outage discrimination in alerting.
No data/tenant/RLS, secret, or language-rule concerns introduced by this delta.

MINOR: Test coverage gap: the delta replaces the only bare `"x509: ..."` case with `"prefix x509: ..."`, so the `^` branch of `x509StringMarker` is no longer exercised; dropping `^` would silently misclassify leading x509 errors.

The new `tls_error` check in `TestAuthorityFailureMetricUsesBoundedReasons` is a source grep of `main.go`, not a runtime assertion; it can miss constructed or other-file emitters and can false-fail on unrelated comments.
NIT: The regex boundary `[^a-z0-9]` also treats `_`, `-`, and `.` as separators, so `not_x509:`/`not.x509:` still map to `db_unavailable`; the anchor only fixes alphanumeric prefixes.
The runbook note states cert failures collapse to `db_unavailable` but gives no concrete log field/query to separate identity/CA from endpoint outages, leaving manual triage underspecified.
SUMMARY: Delta is small and addresses the prior x509 anchoring and retired `tls_error` literal concerns; no blockers or majors found.
Main residual risk is test evidence quality: leading `x509:` classification and runtime absence of `tls_error` are not actually pinned.
Minor regex-boundary and runbook specificity issues remain; AC-2/3/4 are untouched by this delta.

MAJOR: main.go regex change `(^|[^a-z0-9])x509:` → `(^|[\s:])x509:` narrows matching so punctuation-wrapped cert errors (e.g. `(x509:`, `[x509:`, `"x509:`, `- x509:`) now fall through to `internal_error` instead of `db_unavailable`; common `fmt.Errorf`/join wrapping styles regress classification (AC-1 correctness, not cardinality).

This contradicts the runbook line edited in the same delta ("TLS/certificate failures are reported as `db_unavailable`"), so the documented triage query and the classifier can now disagree; no test pins punctuation-wrapped forms.
MINOR: main_test.go adds `x509: leading` and `not_x509:` cases but no `"(x509: ...)"`/`"[x509: ...]"` case, so the narrowing itself is untested in both directions.

Deleting the `tls_error` source grep leaves AC-1 without an evident runtime assertion for the retired reason in this hunk; ensure the gauge assertion compares the full bounded reason label set (extra label = failure), otherwise a reintroduced `tls_error` passes silently.
Verify `os` import in main_test.go is still used after removing the only `os.ReadFile` in that test, otherwise the package will not compile.

Two classification mechanisms coexist (`dbUnavailableMarkers` substring list and `x509StringMarker` regex) with different boundary semantics for the same input; consolidate or document the precedence so a failure cannot be classified by whichever check happens to run.
NIT: `\s` inside `[\s:]` also accepts tab/newline/CR, which is desirable for joined errors but worth a one-line comment since the boundary rule is non-obvious.
Runbook query guidance lists `x509`/`certificate`/`tls handshake`/`pg_hba`; add the `internal_error`-with-x509 case so operators notice the misclassification gap above.
SUMMARY: Delta is small and the AC-negative test for `not_x509:` is a good addition; prior MINOR/NIT items are partially addressed.

Main risk: the boundary tightening trades one false-positive class for a real false-negative class (wrapped cert errors no longer `db_unavailable`), which weakens the operator triage contract this item exists to harden.
Secondary risk: AC-1 evidence for the retired `tls_error` reason now depends on a runtime reason-set assertion that is not visible in the delta.

MAJOR: none (prior MAJOR on regex narrowing and runbook divergence is resolved by this delta: `(`/`[`/`-`-prefixed forms now classify as `db_unavailable`, and the boundary excludes `_ . -` prefixes as the runbook implies).
MINOR: The new boundary class `[^a-zA-Z0-9_.-]` accepts *any* non-alphanumeric separator, so `foo/x509:`, `foo=x509:`, `foo"x509:`, `foo:x509:` now map to `db_unavailable` where they previously were `internal_error`; only `(`, `[`, space and `-` are pinned in tests, so the broadened acceptance set is untested in the positive direction for most separators (AC-1 classifier surface).

No negative test for the widened class: e.g. an embedded token in unrelated error text preceded by punctuation (e.g. `result/x509: ...` from a non-cert source) is now classified `db_unavailable`, which can mask genuine `internal_error` signals; add at least one adversarial case documenting this trade-off.

Negation is ASCII-only: a Unicode letter preceding the token (e.g. `éx509:`) is treated as a boundary and maps to `db_unavailable` despite being part of a word; low risk but worth a one-line rationale or explicit test.
NIT: Case sensitivity is unchanged (`X509:` uppercase still yields `internal_error`); since the regex is being reworked in this delta, add a comment or case so the intended case posture is documented rather than incidental.
Add a one-line comment on the boundary class rationale (why `.`/`_`/`-` are treated as word-continuations) — the rule is non-obvious and future edits are likely.
SUMMARY: Delta is tightly scoped, correct in intent, and fixes the prior wrapped-x509 misclassification while preserving the bounded reason set; no integrity, security, tenant, migration or language-rule issues.
Residual risk is limited to classifier false-positives from the intentionally broad separator class, which is currently only partially pinned by tests.
Recommend merge after adding one or two boundary tests/comments; no blockers.

BLOCKER: The delta adds `{fmt.Errorf("X509: uppercase"), "db_unavailable"}` with no production change in this delta to make the reason classifier case-insensitive; prior review recorded uppercase `X509:` still mapped to `internal_error`, so this is a failing/contradictory regression test.
SUMMARY: Delta is test-only and adds separator/uppercase coverage.
Separator cases are consistent with the widened boundary class, but the uppercase expectation is unsupported by the diff.
Resolve the uppercase test/implementation mismatch before merge; no other new delta findings.

SUMMARY: Delta is a small, safe hardening of reason-code normalization; prior uppercase-`X509` blocker appears resolved via explicit lowercasing.
Residual risk: classification remains message-string dependent (brittle across driver/version changes) and the low-cardinality gauge guarantee is not directly asserted.
